author: Glass Reflection
description:
Time travel in anime usually gives characters the ultimate shortcut, but what happens when a character is forced to take "the long way around"? When one person skips ahead while another has to live through decades, centuries, or even two millennia, that experience needs to leave a mark.

In this video, we break down why this trope works so brilliantly in shows like Mushoku Tensei and Steins;Gate, where aging and time deeply alter a character’s identity and motivation—and why That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime completely stumbles with Chloe’s 2,000-year loop. We’ll also briefly look at Frieren: Beyond Journey's End and long-lived immortal beings to explore what 2,000 years should actually do to a character’s psychology, and why time without narrative consequence feels like a meaningless stat in a character's lore.
